 King, Smith calling on 12th man for home leg vs Antigua-Barbuda

 Trinidad and Tobago captain Denzil Smith has promised supporters a strong performance against Antigua and Barbuda in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League Play-In match-up at the Hasely Crawford Stadium tonight, as the Soca Warriors look to complete the job and advance to the next phase of the CONCACAF Gold Cup qualification process.
 Head coach Derek King also stressed the importance of securing a place in next summer’s Gold Cup, describing the tournament as the closest thing to the World Cup for the national team.
 With T&T holding a slender 3–2 advantage from Thursday night’s first leg, the Warriors will need to avoid another dip in performance when the teams meet in the return fixture, which kicks off at 8 p.m.
 “We need this. This is very important for us to qualify for the Gold Cup,” King said. “The Gold Cup is the closest thing for us to the World Cup. It’s important that we be there come next summer.”
 Smith, who has been entrusted with the captaincy at the age of 27, said the players were eager to deliver a performance that would secure the three points and carry T&T into the next round.
 If the aggregate score is level after the two-leg tie, the away goals rule come into play as the first tie-breaker. T&T scored three away goals.
 If the aggregate and away goals are level at the end of the second leg’s regulation time, 30 minutes of extra time will be played and if still remaining deadlocked, the series would be decided via a penalty shootout.
 The winners will advance to the 14-team CONCACAF Gold Cup Preliminary Round. Seven team will advance from the Prelims to the Gold Cup.
 “At the age of 27, I never knew I would be the captain, but the coach gave me the responsibility to do it. This Monday coming, I’m going to make sure the boys go out there and put on a good showing to make sure we take our three points to head into the next rounds,” he said.
 The captain also promised that the team would give supporters something to cheer about, while appealing for the public to get behind the young squad. “I promise them tomorrow (today), we will put on a good show,” Smith declared.
 The Warriors will enter the contest as favourites, but Thursday’s encounter in Antigua exposed shortcomings that King will be keen to see addressed.
 Although T&T secured their first victory under King after nine successive defeats, their failure to maintain control after taking a seemingly comfortable 3–1 half-time lead was a major concern.
 Antigua and Barbuda pulled one back in stoppage time to reduce the deficit to 3–2, leaving the Warriors with work to do in front of their home supporters.
 King said the coaching staff had reviewed the performance, paying particular attention to the team’s loss of discipline and structure in the second half.
 “When we analysed our first game, what we saw when we led 3–1 at half-time, and we went out there in the second half, our discipline out there, the structure was a bit off,” he said. “Yes, we spoke to them concerning that second half because that was unacceptable at the international level. We have to play for 90-plus.”
 King believes the players understand what is at stake and is expecting a more committed display from the opening whistle. “We took all the positives from our last game, and we continue to work on areas where we have to improve. I think, (today) you will see a team that is willing to go there and execute our game plan and win the game,” he said.
 The coach also warned that Antigua and Barbuda remain dangerous from set-pieces and on the counter-attack, two areas that caused T&T problems in the first encounter. He credited his backroom staff for working to address those weaknesses, while appealing to supporters at home to rally behind the team.
 Smith echoed that call, saying the players needed the public to provide the encouragement that home support can bring.
 “We need that 12th man behind us. If you go and play football in any other country, you will see they have that 12th man behind them. We really need that,” he said.
 King acknowledged that managing the fitness of some of his overseas-based players remained a challenge, with Levi Garcia not fully fit and the length of his travel back to the Caribbean. Rio Cardines is also nursing an injury, while Kobi Henry has been experiencing fatigue.
 However, the coach is confident his young squad can rise to the occasion and deliver the result T&T need to keep their Gold Cup hopes on track.
